title: In Hebrews 1 What Does It Mean For Christ To Be The Exact Representation Of Gods Being
paragraphs: Understanding Hebrews 1: Christ as the Exact Representation of God's Being

Hebrews 1 is a profound declaration of the supremacy of Christ. The writer of Hebrews opens his letter by emphasizing the unique and exalted identity of Jesus. One of the most powerful statements in this chapter is found in verse 3:

who being the effulgence of his glory, and the very image of his substance, and upholding all things by the word of his power, when he had made purification of sins, sat down on the right hand of the Majesty on high; - Hebrews 1:3 ASV
1. The Meaning of "Exact Representation"

The phrase "the very image of his substance" (ASV) or "exact representation of his being" (other translations) uses the Greek word charaktēr. This term originally referred to the impression made by a seal or stamp—an exact imprint or representation. In this context, it means that Christ perfectly reveals and expresses the nature and essence of God.
Fullness of Deity:
Jesus is not merely a reflection of God, but fully possesses and displays all that God is. This echoes what Paul writes in Colossians:
for in him dwelleth all the fulness of the Godhead bodily, - Colossians 2:9 ASV
Visible Image of the Invisible God:
Jesus makes the unseen God visible to us:
who is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of all creation; - Colossians 1:15 ASV
Revealing the Father:
Jesus himself declared that seeing Him is seeing the Father:
Jesus saith unto him, Have I been so long time with you, and dost thou not know me, Philip? he that hath seen me hath seen the Father; how sayest thou, Show us the Father? - John 14:9 ASV
2. Theological Implications
This teaching carries profound significance:

The Deity of Christ: Jesus is not a lesser being or a created angel; He is fully God, sharing the same essence and nature as the Father. This is a foundational truth affirmed throughout the New Testament (John 1:1 ASV).
God’s Final Word: Hebrews 1:1-2 emphasizes that while God spoke through prophets in the past, He has now spoken through His Son, who perfectly reveals God’s will and character.

Salvation Through Christ: Only one who is truly God can offer a perfect sacrifice for sin and reconcile us to the Father. Christ’s unique identity qualifies Him as the sole mediator between God and humanity (1 Timothy 2:5 ASV).
3. Christ’s Ongoing Work

Hebrews 1:3 also speaks of Christ "upholding all things by the word of his power" and "sitting down at the right hand of the Majesty on high." This indicates His continuous work in sustaining creation and His exalted place of authority, a role that belongs to God alone.
And he is before all things, and in him all things consist. - Colossians 1:17 ASV
4. Application: Knowing God Through Christ

Since Jesus is the exact representation of God’s being, to know Christ is to know God. Our understanding of God’s character, love, holiness, and purpose is found most clearly in the person and work of Jesus. Therefore, as believers, we are called to fix our eyes on Jesus as the perfect revelation of God.

looking unto Jesus the author and perfecter of our faith, who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising shame, and hath sat down at the right hand of the throne of God. - Hebrews 12:2 ASV
Summary

Hebrews 1 declares that Jesus is the "exact representation of God’s being," meaning He fully and perfectly reveals who God is. This truth affirms Christ’s deity, His authority, and His role as the perfect Savior. Knowing Jesus is knowing God, and in Him we see the fullness of God’s glory and grace.
